frame: Robot frame: origin on the ground under the centre of the front axle; x forward, y left, z up. Lengths in mm unless the unit says otherwise.

provenance_classes.measured: Read directly off a recording of a real Vector made by this household (source REC), with no model in between. simulacrum/recording.py recomputes each one from the recording's files. Must cite REC. One robot, one run: a measured value is a fact about that run, not about every Vector.
provenance_classes.fitted: Chosen by a fit to the recording (source REC): by fit_recording.py so that the model reproduces named segments, or by simulacrum/imu_fit.py for the accelerometer's steady offsets. A fit is not a measurement: it depends on the shape of what was fitted and, for fit_recording.py, on the assumed values in place when it ran. The source says what it was fitted to and what was held out. Must cite REC and carry low and high.
provenance_classes.manual: Stated in the Vector Technical Reference Manual (source TRM).
provenance_classes.sdk: Published by the vendor in software, or fixed in household SDK-level code. source_kind says which: vendor_firmware (released robot source), vendor_webots_model (Anki's own Webots simulation model), vendor_sdk (the Python SDK the recorder runs), household_code (limits in vector-slam-maze), vendor_animation_rig (Anki's animators' model of the robot, RIG). The vendor marks several of these as approximate; that is carried in note.
provenance_classes.assumed: A property of the robot that the author set with no source that states it. Always carries low and high for randomisation. Each one is a measurement still to be taken.
provenance_classes.chosen: A setting of the scene or of the solver (kind scene or numeric): table size, time step, contact stiffness. Not a claim about the robot, so there is no real value to find; the solver ones are checked for convergence instead.

REC2.what: Recordings of the same Vector on 2026-11-18 by hardware/record_barriered.py, run on the wire-pod host by a lane at its go, at the default control level. Run A: off the charger, 20 s at rest, head and lift over their range. Runs B and C: the cube wheelie phase; the robot found no cube both times (ConnectCube answered success false after about 15 s), so they hold rest rows only. Run D: the dock phase; already on the charger, nothing commanded. Run E: off the charger, 20 s at rest, spins 3.0 s each way at 150 and 220 mm/s; ended clean. Run F: off the charger, 20 s at rest, then the endurance phase: spins at 300 mm/s commanded, 3 s on, 2 s off, both ways, planned 600 s; at about 150 s the robot met a cliff (status bit 0x4000 at 194.42 s), reacted itself and took control (control_lost logged at 195.55 s); 29 full spins. tread_center_spacing_mm.source: RIG: the tread chains are centred at y -23.98 and +23.90 mm, measured by RIG (simulacrum/body_mesh.py, evidence/body-shape). FW:26 WHEEL_DIST_MM = 46 is marked approximate and stays in tread_spacing_mm for the turn arithmetic.
tread_center_spacing_mm.note: Centre to centre of the two treads as built.

tread_spacing_mm.source: FW:26 WHEEL_DIST_MM = 46 ("approx distance b/w the center of the front treads"); WEBOTS:594,730 tracks at y = +/-0.023; GOSIM:28 WheelTrackMm = 46
tread_spacing_mm.note: Centre to centre. The vendor calls it approximate.

tread_width_mm.source: RIG: each tread chain is 11.50 mm wide, measured by RIG (simulacrum/body_mesh.py, evidence/body-shape). Parts printed to fit a real Vector agree: 11.6 mm (Thingiverse 3241305, 3464746, 4287628). WEBOTS:612 had 10.

tread_contact_inset_mm.source: REC2 run-e-spins.jsonl (unit 1, the four spins at 150 and 220 mm/s, both ways). Fitted by simulacrum/spin_fit.py (fit_spins.py): each spin replayed from the robot's recorded head and lift at insets 0 to 8 mm in 1 mm steps; the mean steady turn rate over the second half of each spin, model over robot, both read through the IMU chip's filter (simulacrum/imu_filter.py), is 0.871 at no inset, 0.995 at 3 and 1.040 at 4, so it reaches 1 at 3.10 mm. Fitted one spin at a time (ccw and cw at 150, then at 220) it reaches 1 at 2.88, 3.44, 2.92 and 3.04 mm. Before the model's gyro had the chip's filter the same fit gave 3.01 mm. Held out: unit 3's four camera spins (evidence/camera-spins-unit3-20261120) on the 2.0 table go from 0.83 to 0.86 of the robot's rate at no inset to 1.01 to 1.04 at the fitted inset, and the model's turn centre from x = -21.4 to -25.2 mm to -24.1 to -25.1 mm, against -25.4 to -28.9 mm measured from the camera (simulacrum/camera_spins.py). The ratios step unevenly (0.923 at 1 mm, 0.946 at 2), which is the treads' chatter; the range of 1 mm either way is the author's allowance for that. Refitted 2026-11-22 with the treads as built (tread_width_mm 11.5, tread_center_spacing_mm 47.9) and the head box centred where the rig puts it, on the reference MuJoCo 4.0.1 (Linux x86_64, evidence/body-shape/refit/fit_spins.json): 3.415 mm, per spin 3.34 to 3.53. Unit 3's four held-out spins then turn within 1.61 % RMS (2.19 % with the previous geometry at its own 4.0.1 fit of 3.242 mm) and unit 1's four fitted spins within 1.50 % (0.77 %). On MuJoCo 3.11.0 the same geometry fits 3.168 mm. The fit trades against com_x_mm, which is assumed: a 0.26 mm shift of the centre of mass moved the fitted inset by 0.27 mm.
tread_contact_inset_mm.note: Moves where the treads touch the table, not the axles: the model's four wheels sit this far inside the 48 mm wheel base, while the firmware's odometry keeps the axles. Tipping keeps them too: body-fixed supports round the real axles (tip_support_clearance_mm) take over once the body tilts, so the model balances where wheelstand.py's closed form says. It closes the spin rate and keeps the turn centre where unit 3 turns.

chassis_length_mm.source: RIG: the lower body reaches past the rear axle, to x -66.7 mm (RIG (simulacrum/body_mesh.py, evidence/body-shape)). The box runs from the rear axle (FW:28, x -48) to the front of the Webots body (WEBOTS:146-185, x 13): a box cannot follow the rounded rear without catching early when the robot rears up, which only the real shape (VectorSim(body=...)) does.
chassis_length_mm.note: Collision shape of the lower body only.

chassis_center_x_mm.source: RIG: centre of the box from the rear axle (x -48) to x 13; see chassis_length_mm.

chassis_top_z_mm.source: WEBOTS:97 body centre 0.0142 above the ground, WEBOTS:185 box height 0.026

chassis_ground_clearance_mm.source: RIG: the body's lowest point is 1.23 mm above the table (RIG (simulacrum/body_mesh.py, evidence/body-shape)); WEBOTS:97,185 leaves 1.2 mm.
chassis_ground_clearance_mm.note: Decides whether the belly catches on a table edge.

total_mass_g.source: WEBOTS:91, a commented-out line "#mass 0.17 # about 6 ounces". Retailer listings give about 159 g according to a web search summary; the pages themselves could not be read (HTTP 403 or script-rendered), so that figure only widens the range.

wheel_mass_g.source: No source. Each of the four wheels.

com_x_mm.source: No source states it. Whole robot, lift down, head level. Set to the middle of the wheel base because the firmware puts the turn centre there (FW:62 DRIVE_CENTER_OFFSET = -25) and in this model the turn centre follows the centre of mass.
com_x_mm.note: REC2 run E (2026-11-18, spins at 150 and 220 mm/s, surface not recorded): the robot turned at 184 and 270 deg/s; replayed at -24 the model turns at 0.85-0.90 of that, at -29 at 0.94-1.04, at -30 at 1.03-1.09, at -14 at 1.38-1.49 (replay_recording.py --wheels-of). REC's wheel scores barely move from -24 to -29 (fit 0.167-0.173, held out 0.141-0.145). So this run points to -29 or -30, the end of the range; the value is not changed on one run. The rear wheelstand settles it: -24 predicts 64.9 deg, -29 predicts 59.4.

com_z_mm.source: No source. Whole robot, lift down, head level.

tread_friction.source: No source. Rubber tread on a hard table.

chassis_friction.source: No source. Plastic body on a hard table.

wheel_speed_max_mmps.note: The firmware applies it in path following only (STEERC:419 CheckWheelSpeedLimits), not in direct drive; the model likewise caps drive_straight and the policy's action scale with it, not set_wheel_motors. Sent 300 mm/s by set_wheel_motors the robot reached 243-247 (REC2 run F).

wheel_speed_cliff_safe_mmps.source: FW:299 MAX_SAFE_WHEEL_SPEED_MMPS = 170 ("can the robot drive without falling off (most) straight edge cliffs")
wheel_speed_cliff_safe_mmps.note: Not an input to the model. A figure the model can be checked against.

wheel_stall_torque_mNm.source: REC. Torque of one tread drive at the front wheel at full motor power and zero speed. Fitted by fit_recording.py to REC segments spin_ccw_30, spin_cw_30, spin_ccw_100, spin_cw_100, back_40, forward_40 (reported wheel speeds and gyro z); the 60 mm/s spins and 80 mm/s steps were held out. The range is the author's: one robot, one run. It is fitted with the assumed mass and tread friction in place; the recording fixes how strong the motor is relative to the load, not the torque by itself. Refitted 2026-11-18 (fit_recording.py --wheels-held-noload, twice, 105 then 105 replays) with tread_noload_speed_mmps held where REC2 run F's cold full-power spins put it, after the direct-drive clamp at 220 mm/s was found wrong (STEERC:419 applies it in path following only). Final table: REC fit segments 0.143, held out 0.140 (the table before: 0.170 and 0.143); run F's first spin each way, model 244.2 and 244.1 mm/s against the robot's 247.1 and 243.3 at the SDK's 4.0797 V. Before the refit: 100.0.

tread_noload_speed_mmps.source: REC. Tread speed at full power with no load, for a linear motor. Fitted by fit_recording.py to REC segments spin_ccw_30, spin_cw_30, spin_ccw_100, spin_cw_100, back_40, forward_40 (reported wheel speeds and gyro z); the 60 mm/s spins and 80 mm/s steps were held out. The range is the author's: one robot, one run. The firmware's own feedforward line (WHEELC:101) reads as 319.5; this robot on this surface at 4.0 V gives less speed per unit of power. Refitted 2026-11-18 (fit_recording.py --wheels-held-noload, twice, 105 then 105 replays) with tread_noload_speed_mmps held where REC2 run F's cold full-power spins put it, after the direct-drive clamp at 220 mm/s was found wrong (STEERC:419 applies it in path following only). Final table: REC fit segments 0.143, held out 0.140 (the table before: 0.170 and 0.143); run F's first spin each way, model 244.2 and 244.1 mm/s against the robot's 247.1 and 243.3 at the SDK's 4.0797 V. Before the refit: 265.0. The value is chosen on run F's ceiling (300: 239.9 mm/s, 305: 244.2), not by the descent; REC alone preferred 265.

tread_friction_power_fraction.source: REC. Drive friction as a fraction of stall torque. Fitted by fit_recording.py to REC segments spin_ccw_30, spin_cw_30, spin_ccw_100, spin_cw_100, back_40, forward_40 (reported wheel speeds and gyro z); the 60 mm/s spins and 80 mm/s steps were held out. The range is the author's: one robot, one run. The firmware's line reads as 0.057. Refitted 2026-11-18 (fit_recording.py --wheels-held-noload, twice, 105 then 105 replays) with tread_noload_speed_mmps held where REC2 run F's cold full-power spins put it, after the direct-drive clamp at 220 mm/s was found wrong (STEERC:419 applies it in path following only). Final table: REC fit segments 0.143, held out 0.140 (the table before: 0.170 and 0.143); run F's first spin each way, model 244.2 and 244.1 mm/s against the robot's 247.1 and 243.3 at the SDK's 4.0797 V. Before the refit: 0.1. The range was widened from 0.06-0.15 to hold the refitted value.

wheel_ff_slope_power_per_mmps.source: WHEELC:101 out_ol = 0.00313 * x + 0.057 above 30 mm/s (the hardware branch, not the SIMULATOR one)

wheel_ff_low_slope_power_per_mmps.source: WHEELC:104 out_ol = 0.00666667 * x at or below 30 mm/s. The two branches do not meet at 30 mm/s (0.200 against 0.151).

wheel_command_stopped_mmps.source: WHEELH:18 WHEEL_SPEED_COMMAND_STOPPED_MM_S; WHEELC:164-181: at or below it the power is 0, and power is never applied against the commanded direction

wheel_accel_zero_is_immediate.source: STEERC:520-522: a zero acceleration means "max acceleration (i.e. command target velocity)"

wheel_speed_reported_whole_mmps.source: WHEELC:47-48 the measured wheel speed is an integer (s32); WHEELC:30,220-222 the filter coefficient is 0, so the reported speed is that integer

tread_mm_per_encoder_count.source: HALM:62-63 (0.96 * 29.0 * 0.25 * pi) / 172.3, "Magic 96% corrective fudge factor, 29mm wheel diameter". The source does not say what 172.3 is.
tread_mm_per_encoder_count.note: 7.880 counts per mm. The model takes this as the true tread travel per count.

odometry_wheel_factor.source: HALM:62 the corrective factor inside the encoder scale: the robot's odometry behaves as if the wheel were 27.84 mm across
odometry_wheel_factor.note: Not an input on its own; it is inside tread_mm_per_encoder_count.

encoder_zero_speed_ticks.source: HALM:58 ZERO_SPEED_ENCODER_TIC_THRESH: no new count for this many control ticks reads as zero speed

lift_rad_per_encoder_count.source: HALM:64 (0.25 * pi) / 149.7. The source does not say what 149.7 is.

head_rad_per_encoder_count.source: HALM:65 (0.25 * pi) / 366.211. The source does not say what 366.211 is.

wheel_armature_gcm2.source: REC. Rotor inertia seen at each wheel joint through the gearbox. Fitted by fit_recording.py to REC segments spin_ccw_30, spin_cw_30, spin_ccw_100, spin_cw_100, back_40, forward_40 (reported wheel speeds and gyro z); the 60 mm/s spins and 80 mm/s steps were held out. The range is the author's: one robot, one run. With the stall torque it sets how fast the treads speed up and stop. Refitted 2026-11-18 (fit_recording.py --wheels-held-noload, twice, 105 then 105 replays) with tread_noload_speed_mmps held where REC2 run F's cold full-power spins put it, after the direct-drive clamp at 220 mm/s was found wrong (STEERC:419 applies it in path following only). Final table: REC fit segments 0.143, held out 0.140 (the table before: 0.170 and 0.143); run F's first spin each way, model 244.2 and 244.1 mm/s against the robot's 247.1 and 243.3 at the SDK's 4.0797 V. Before the refit: 2000.0.

body_rotation_speed_observed_dps.source: FW:307 comment: "It can actually spin closer to 360 deg/s" at full wheel speed
body_rotation_speed_observed_dps.note: Not an input. A figure the model can be checked against.

spin_rate_fraction_measured.source: REC table-run1.jsonl, recording.spin_ratios: turn rate over the no-slip rate (wheel speed difference over tread spacing) in the second half of the six recorded spins at 30, 60 and 100 mm/s: 0.49, 0.51, 0.49, 0.53, 0.44 and 0.52, mean 0.497 (13 to 22 samples each). The gyro is in the head and the head was 22.4 deg up in all six, so gyro z alone reads 0.41 to 0.50 (mean 0.46); the figure here is from gyro x and z together. Clockwise was faster than counter-clockwise in all three pairs.
spin_rate_fraction_measured.note: Not an input. A figure the model can be checked against. One robot, one surface, head up; nothing above 100 mm/s was held.

drive_center_offset_mm.source: FW:62 DRIVE_CENTER_OFFSET = -25 on the robot (FW:59 gives -16 in the vendor simulator)
drive_center_offset_mm.note: Not an input. Where the robot turns about is an outcome of the model.

encoder_tread_direction_sensed.source: TRM 11.4.5, trm.txt:2370-2372: the tread motors have a single emitter and detector; TRM 11, trm.txt:2040-2043: a Sharp GP1S092HCPIF on the tread motors, a dual-channel part on lift and head
encoder_tread_direction_sensed.note: The reported wheel speed takes its sign from the command.

head_camera_position_mm.source: FW:120 HEAD_CAM_POSITION, relative to the neck joint

imu_position_mm.source: FW:126 IMU_POSITION, relative to the neck joint
imu_position_mm.note: The IMU is in the head (TRM 63.2.2, trm.txt:12037; IMUCPP:876 subtracts the head angle to get pitch). REC confirms its axes turn with the head: gyro x over gyro z follows tan(head angle) with slope 0.9985 over 369 turning samples (recording.gyro_frame). See imu_pitch_offset_deg.

imu_pitch_offset_deg.source: REC table-run1.jsonl, simulacrum/imu_fit.py, the same fit as accel_bias_mg: with the reported head angle at 0 on a level surface the accelerometer's frame is pitched -0.66 deg (nose down), standard error 0.17 deg; leaving out each cluster of head angle gives -0.64 to -0.81. An independent signal agrees in sign and size: recording.gyro_frame fits gyro x over gyro z against tan(head angle) over 369 turning samples and finds slope 0.9985 and an offset of -1.06 deg. The range spans both.
imu_pitch_offset_deg.note: The sum of the body's stance on its treads, the mounting of the part and any zero error of the head angle; the recording cannot separate them. The model applies it to the IMU's frame.

head_box_center_wrt_neck_mm.source: RIG: centre of the head's extent relative to neck_joint_position_mm, head level (RIG (simulacrum/body_mesh.py, evidence/body-shape)).

head_box_mm.source: RIG: extent of the head with the head level, -31.39 to 8.35 mm along x, 46.36 mm across, 30.58 to 69.33 mm high, measured by RIG (simulacrum/body_mesh.py, evidence/body-shape). The box replaced one drawn round the capsules of WEBOTS:307-425.

head_accel_default_radps2.source: SDKPY:683 set_head_angle(..., accel: float = 10.0, max_speed: float = 10.0); the recorder calls it with the defaults
head_accel_default_radps2.note: The model ramps the head's commanded angle up and down at this rate, capped by head_speed_max_radps. Whether the firmware does exactly this is not stated; it is the reading that reproduces the longer moves' higher speeds in REC and REC2 run A (see servo_command_delay_ms).

head_servo_kp_mNm_per_rad.source: No source. Stands in for the firmware position loop.

servo_armature_gcm2.source: No source. Head and lift rotor inertia at the joint.

camera_fov_vertical_deg.source: TRM 79.2, trm.txt:15732-15733: the cropped image has a 90 degree horizontal and 50 degree vertical field of view

display_resolution_px.source: VICOSLCD: the SANTEK panel used when hw_ver is 1..7 (Vector 1.0); VDOCS agrees

lift_fork_side_center_mm.source: Symmetric wrist-relative contact proxies inside the outer side plates of Dauler forks7.stl, Thingiverse 3731746; stock fork outline cross-checked in iFixit guide 123280

lift_fork_side_size_mm.source: Conservative solid portion of the two printable fork side plates, excluding clips and the curved bottom corners. Original hardware contact dimensions unmeasured.

lift_accel_default_radps2.source: SDKPY:753 set_lift_height(..., accel: float = 10.0, max_speed: float = 10.0); the recorder calls it with the defaults
lift_accel_default_radps2.note: As head_accel_default_radps2, for the lift arm's angle.

cliff_front_x_mm.source: FW:210 kCliffSensorXOffsetFront_mm = 2 ("approximate and should be verified"); WEBOTS:114 has 0

cliff_y_mm.source: FW:209 kCliffSensorYOffset_mm = 14 (approximate); WEBOTS:114 has 15; GOSIM:31 has 12

cliff_sensor_height_mm.source: No source. The vendor Webots model puts the sensors 1.2 mm above the ground (WEBOTS:97,114).

cliff_detect_range_mm.source: No source. Distance from sensor to surface beyond which a cliff is reported. The real sensor reports infrared brightness against a threshold (FW:199-205), not a distance.

cliff_values_exposed.source: TRM 26, trm.txt:4236-4239: "The individual sensor values are not accessible"; one status bit covers all four

cliff_reaction_backup_mm.source: REC, one event, by the robot's own odometry: from where it stopped (229.26, 53.65) to where it came to rest (201.50, 62.66) is 29.2 mm. It then turned about 170 degrees to face the edge, which the model does not do. Other sources: GOSIM:33 has 40; CLIFFJSON:7 has 60; CLIFFCPP:798 says the animation backs up about 80.

cliff_reaction_backup_speed_mmps.source: REC, one event: reported wheel speeds of 210, 178, 224 and 206 mm/s in the two rows of the move away (mean 205). CLIFFJSON:8 has 100 for a later recovery move.

cliff_event_delay_ms.source: FW:331 CLIFF_EVENT_DELAY_MS = 500 ("between stopping the motors and issuing a cliff event")
cliff_event_delay_ms.note: Not an input. The first two versions used it as the pause before the back-up.

tof_position_mm.source: FW:68 kProxSensorPosition_mm ("TODO: finalize these dimensions on production robot")

tof_fov_deg.note: Modelled since 2026-11-18: a fan of 19 rays across this cone (simulacrum/prox.py RINGS).

tof_range_min_mm.source: TRM 11.4.2, trm.txt:2341: usable range 30 mm to 1200 mm

tof_useful_max_mm.source: TRM 11.4.2, trm.txt:2342: "max useful range closer to 300mm for Vector"

control_period_ms.source: TRM 114.3, trm.txt:19985: the motor control loops "are updated 200 times per second"; FW:324 ROBOT_TIME_STEP_MS = 5 agrees

state_period_ms.source: REC: the interval between state messages as the SDK receives them. Median 59.8 ms, mean 60.0 ms over 2,699 intervals awake; median 59.9 ms over 333 intervals asleep on the charger. The firmware sends its own state every 30 ms (FW:383); the SDK stream is half that rate.

state_period_firmware_ms.note: Not an input. The SDK receives state every 60 ms (state_period_ms).

command_delay_ms.source: REC. Time from the host issuing a wheel command to the treads acting on it, with the return path of the state message folded in: the recording cannot separate the two. Fitted by fit_recording.py to REC segments spin_ccw_30, spin_cw_30, spin_ccw_100, spin_cw_100, back_40, forward_40 (reported wheel speeds and gyro z); the 60 mm/s spins and 80 mm/s steps were held out. The range is the author's: one robot, one run. Refitted 2026-11-18 with the other tread values (see tread_noload_speed_mmps): 60 -> 75 ms.

turn_tolerance_deg.source: TRM 62.9.1, trm.txt:11942-11944: the angular tolerance "is clamped to a minimum of 2 degrees internally"
turn_tolerance_deg.note: A turn in place ends when the remaining angle is inside this.

head_power_gains.unit: motor power per rad: Kp, Ki, Kd
head_power_gains.note: Not an input. The gains are in motor power, and how much torque a unit of power gives the head motor is not published. The model's head drive stays assumed.

lift_power_gains.unit: motor power per rad: Kp, Ki, Kd
lift_power_gains.note: Not an input, for the same reason.

imu_part.source: IMUCPP:153 a comment cites the "BMI160 datasheet"; VDOCS (a community page) lists "IMU: BMI160". The manual does not name the part.

gyro_noise_rms_dps.source: REC rest-on-charger.jsonl: standard deviation 0.032, 0.036 and 0.032 deg/s on the three axes over 334 rows (79 distinct samples), robot asleep on the charger. Awake and moving it will be more. The BMI160 datasheet gives 0.07 (BMI160DS:527-530).

gyro_bias_dps.source: REC table-run1.jsonl, recording.gyro_at_rest: mean reading over every still stretch (695 rows in 31 stretches, 7 s to 155 s) is 0.0006, 0.0086 and -0.0010 deg/s. This is what is left after the firmware's own bias removal (IMUCPP:102 accepts estimates within a 0.35 deg/s band); the part's raw zero-rate offset is +/-3 deg/s (BMI160DS:503). The largest mean of any one still stretch is 0.038 deg/s, and the range is that.
gyro_bias_dps.note: Measured only while still. Whether the firmware's estimate drifts during long motion is not in the recording.

accel_noise_rms_mg.source: REC rest-on-charger.jsonl: standard deviation 13.5, 11.5 and 12.1 mm/s^2 on the three axes (mean 12.4 mm/s^2) over 334 rows, robot asleep on the charger. The BMI160 datasheet gives 1.8 mg (BMI160DS:442-444).

accel_bias_mg.source: REC table-run1.jsonl, simulacrum/imu_fit.py: least squares over the 26 still stretches on the table (625 rows) for the table's tilt, the pitch of the accelerometer's frame and one offset per axis, in a model of the accelerometer alone (the MuJoCo model is not involved). Offsets -47.0, -7.7 and +22.3 mg; the fit's own standard errors are 3.0, 0.6 and 0.4 mg, the residual is 17 mm/s^2 rms, and leaving out each cluster of head angle in turn moves them by at most 1.2 mg. Nothing else was held out. The x offset and imu_pitch_offset_deg trade against each other (correlation -0.98 in the fit): a bootstrap over the still stretches puts x between -48.9 and -45.1 mg and their sum, the x reading on a level surface at head angle 0, between -60.3 and -57.3 mg. The two are drawn independently in training, which is wider than the fit allows. Gravity is taken as 9806.65 mm/s^2, which leaves about 3 mg of doubt on z; the y offset cannot be told from a roll of the frame. The range of +/-10 mg is the author's allowance for those and for temperature. BMI160DS:410 gives +/-40 mg for the part, so x on this robot is outside the part's typical figure.
accel_bias_mg.note: A fact about one robot. Another Vector will have other offsets; widen the range to +/-40 mg per axis to train for any unit.

accel_scale.source: The part's nominal sensitivity, 16384 LSB/g at +/-2 g; BMI160DS:390-393 gives 15729 to 17039 LSB/g, 0.960 to 1.040 of nominal, which is the range. Each axis's reading of the true specific force is multiplied by its scale before the offset (accel_bias_mg) is added. On this robot the x scale is not settled: simulacrum/imu_fit.py with the scale freed over REC table-run1.jsonl (26 still stretches) gives 1.0118, standard error 0.0044, while the another substrate's fit over table-run1 and run A (the lab's coordination room turn 166) gave 0.999 and found no held-out gain; that fit shared one tilt between the two runs' surfaces, which pulls the scale toward 1 (its author, turn 195). Run A alone cannot be fitted: it has one heading, so the table's tilt cannot be told from the offsets. The value stays nominal until a run settles it. y and z are not identifiable from these recordings (see the 2.0 table's entry).
accel_scale.note: A per-unit fact; unit 3 (a 2.0) fits 1.014 on x.

accel_filter_cutoff_hz.source: The -3 dB point of the chip's accelerometer filter as the firmware sets it: IMUC:132 ACC_RATE_200HZ 0x19, written to ACC_CONF at IMUC:241, is acc_us 0, acc_bwp 0b001 (OSR2) and acc_odr 0b1001 (200 Hz) by the layout at BMI160DS:3285-3310. BMI160DS:1044-1048 gives 80 Hz at 200 Hz in normal mode on all three axes, and BMI160DS:1075-1080 says OSR2 halves it: 40 Hz. A part datasheet's figure, so assumed. It states no tolerance; the range of 10% each way is a guess, not a figure from it.
accel_filter_cutoff_hz.note: Applied by simulacrum/imu_filter.py at every physics step; the state message carries the latest raw sample (MSGCPP:94-97).

gyro_filter_cutoff_hz.source: The -3 dB point of the chip's gyro filter as the firmware sets it: IMUC:134 GYRO_RATE_200HZ_OVS_4X 0x09, written to GYR_CONF at IMUC:244, is gyr_bwp 0b00 (OSR4) and gyr_odr 0b1001 (200 Hz) by the layout at BMI160DS:3379-3393. BMI160DS:1143 gives 74.6 Hz at 200 Hz in normal mode, and BMI160DS:1160-1165 says OSR4 makes it approximately four times smaller: 18.65 Hz. A part datasheet's figure, so assumed. It states no tolerance; the range of 10% each way is a guess, not a figure from it.
gyro_filter_cutoff_hz.note: Applied by simulacrum/imu_filter.py at every physics step. Nothing after the chip filters again: MSGCPP:94-100 puts the latest sample, less the gyro's bias estimate (IMUCPP:950), in the state message.

imu_filter_second_pole.source: The shape of the chip's filter, which no source states. BMI160DS:1075 and 1153-1160 say that in OSR2 and OSR4 "both stages of the digital filter are used", and give neither stage's shape. simulacrum/imu_filter.py models them as two one-pole sections in series, -3 dB together at each cutoff; this is the lower corner over the higher. 1 is two equal sections, taken because nothing favours either stage; 0 is one section alone. A stage of higher order than one is outside the range.

cube_outer_mm.source: No vendor source states the cube's outside. Two parts printed to fit a real cube measure 45.0 mm (Thingiverse 3239449, a battery cap; 3405048, a dummy cube box), as does the Webots Block1x1 used for the cube's mass. Anki's animation cube is 42.2 mm. BLOCKDEF:6 gives 44 mm, the size the engine gives the cube it sees.

cube_size_mm.source: BLOCKDEF:6 START_BLOCK_DEFINITION(LIGHTCUBE1, (44.f,44.f,44.f), ORANGE); LIGHTCUBE2 at BLOCKDEF:16 is the same. The size the engine gives the cube it sees and carries, not a measurement of unit 3's cube.

cube_carry_offset_mm.source: CARRY:245-246 puts a carried object's centre at (the docking marker's distance from the centre + LIFT_FRONT_WRT_WRIST_JOINT, 0, -12.5) from the lift pose. The marker is on a face, half of BLOCKDEF:6's 44 mm out, and FW:105 gives LIFT_FRONT_WRT_WRIST_JOINT = 4: 22 + 4 = 26. The lift pose is the wrist, level: LIFTPOSE fullRobotPose.cpp:48 places it LIFT_ARM_LENGTH along the arm and LIFTPOSE:1532-1541 undoes the arm's rotation.
cube_carry_offset_mm.note: The cube's centre from the wrist joint, on the level fork's axes. Used when the model carries a cube (mjcf.py).

cube_chip_position_mm.source: No source: where the accelerometer sits in the cube, from its centre, on the cube's axes as carried. The cube is 44 mm across (BLOCKDEF:6), so the chip is within 22 mm of the centre on each axis; 15 mm leaves room for the case and is a guess. The spin test with the cube measures the horizontal part (README).

cube_chip_yaw_deg.source: No source: the turn about vertical from the robot's x axis to the chip's, as carried. Which face the robot carries forward varies, and where the chip's axes point inside the cube is not known. The chip's z is taken as the cube's vertical because the tap detector watches z alone (CUBEACC:124); that is an inference, not checked. The spin test with the cube measures this angle.

cube_accel_range_g.source: CUBEACC:82 spi_write8(PMU_RANGE, 0x05) "+4g range"; BMA253DS:897 (Table 5) range 0101 is +/-4g.

cube_accel_word_format.source: BMA253DS:832-842 documents the upper 12 bits. The nominal model fills the remaining four bits with zero.

cube_accel_counts_per_g.source: CUBETOOL:66 const ONEG = 0x2000, the divisor Anki's tool applies to the int16 it reads. BMA253DS:384 gives 512 LSB/g at +/-4 g, and BMA253DS:832-835 puts the 12 bits at the top of the 16 (bits 11 to 4 in the MSB, 3 to 0 at the top of the LSB): 512 x 16 = 8192. The engine divides by 32767/4 instead (cubeAccelComponent.cpp).

cube_accel_bandwidth_hz.source: CUBEACC:83 spi_write8(PMU_BW, 0x0D) "250hz BW"; BMA253DS:866 (Table 4) bw 01101 is 250 Hz, and BMA253DS:404-407 call the filter "2nd order". A part datasheet's figure, so assumed. BMA253DS:1286 refers to tolerances on the bandwidths that this extraction does not show; 10% each way is a guess.

cube_accel_frame_period_ms.source: BMA253DS:845-847: the filtered data's sampling rate "is always twice the selected bandwidth (BW = ODR/2)"; BMA253DS:866 (Table 4) gives an update time of 2 ms at 250 Hz. CUBEACC:83's comment says "1000 samples per second", which the datasheet contradicts, and the tap detector's "90ms" (CUBEACC:101) is 90 frames, so 180 ms. The chip clock's tolerance is not stated; 10% each way is a guess.

cube_accel_filter_second_pole.source: BMA253DS:404: the bandwidth filter is "2nd order"; its shape is not stated. As imu_filter_second_pole: two one-pole sections in series, -3 dB together at the bandwidth, this the lower corner over the higher; 1 is two equal sections. Below 0.5 the second section would hardly count, which a second-order filter rules out; that bound is a judgement.

cube_accel_noise_axis_scale.source: Equal axis noise assumed for cubes without a stationary recording.
cube_accel_noise_axis_scale.note: Effective noise multiplier before filtering. Bounds are sensitivity limits.

cube_accel_noise_density_ug.source: BMA253DS:413-415: output noise density 220 typical, in the +/-2 g range, normal mode, nominal supplies. The cube runs +/-4 g. A datasheet typical, so assumed; the range is a guess.
cube_accel_noise_density_ug.note: Injected as white noise before the chip filter (simulacrum/cube.py).

cube_accel_bias_mg.source: BMA253DS:395-396: zero-g offset +/-80 mg typical over life-time (+/-2 g range, 25 C); +/-20 mg before soldering (BMA253DS:391-392). 0 is the nominal. Still recordings of the cube resting on each face would measure it.

cube_accel_scale.source: BMA253DS:383-387 give the nominal sensitivity only, with no tolerance in this extraction; 3% each way is a guess. Still recordings of the cube on each face would measure it.

cube_tick_ms.source: CUBEIMPL:79-82: app_tick runs the app's tick and then re-arms app_easy_timer(1, app_tick); EASYTIMER:83: the delay counts "timer slots (10 ms)". Re-arming after the tick makes the true period longer by the tick's own run time.
cube_tick_ms.note: A recording by hardware/cube_accel.py gives the true period: one message per three ticks.

tof_range_std_fraction.source: REC rest-on-charger.jsonl: standard deviation 5.2 mm at a mean of 237 mm over 334 rows, one distance and one target. That noise grows in proportion to distance is the model's form, not measured. The VL53L0X datasheet gives 3 to 7% (VL53DS:1260-1267).

tof_report_min_mm.source: ENGPROX:92 kMinObsThreshold_mm; the reported distance is clamped to it (ENGPROX:173). The lowest distance in the 9929 recorded rows is 30.

tof_report_max_mm.source: ENGPROX:93 kMaxObsThreshold_mm; the reported distance is clamped to it (ENGPROX:173). The highest distance in the 9929 recorded rows is 400.

tof_quality_min.source: ENGPROX:96 kMinQualityThreshold: at or below it the reading counts as hitting nothing (ENGPROX:175-178).

tof_lift_occluding_min_mm.source: ENGPROX:49 kLiftHeightOccludingProxSensorMin: from this lift height the lift is in the beam.

tof_lift_occluding_max_mm.source: ENGPROX:50 kLiftHeightOccludingProxSensorMax. In REC2, 111 of the 205 rows with the lift between these heights read the minimum distance.

tof_lift_clear_ms.source: ENGPROX:42-46 kMinNumConsecTicsLiftOutOfFOV = 3 robot state messages of 30 ms: the lift counts as in view until it has been out for that long.

tof_lift_distance_mm.source: ENGPROX:69 kLiftSensorDistance_mm: how far the lift is from the sensor when it is in the beam.

tof_found_pitch_limit_deg.source: ENGPROX:57-58 kMinPitch, kMaxPitch: outside this pitch nothing counts as a found object (ENGPROX:181-182).

tof_quality_at_100mm.source: REC, REC2. Fitted by simulacrum/prox_fit.py to all 9929 state rows of the nine recordings that carry the sensor's distance and signal quality (one robot; what stood in front of it is not known). Signal quality of a return from 100 mm: the line through log quality against log distance over the 4776 rows with quality above tof_quality_min, a distance inside the report limits and the lift out of the beam. Nothing held out. The scatter about the line is more than a factor of ten (at 80-120 mm the middle 80% of rows run from 0.012 to 0.45).

tof_quality_distance_exponent.source: REC, REC2. Fitted by simulacrum/prox_fit.py to all 9929 state rows of the nine recordings that carry the sensor's distance and signal quality (one robot; what stood in front of it is not known). Slope of the same line: quality falls as distance to this power. An inverse square law would be -2.

tof_quality_floor.source: REC, REC2. Fitted by simulacrum/prox_fit.py to all 9929 state rows of the nine recordings that carry the sensor's distance and signal quality (one robot; what stood in front of it is not known). Median signal quality of the 4713 rows with quality at or below tof_quality_min: what the sensor reports with no usable return.

tof_weak_distance_mm.source: REC, REC2. Fitted by simulacrum/prox_fit.py to all 9929 state rows of the nine recordings that carry the sensor's distance and signal quality (one robot; what stood in front of it is not known). Median reported distance of those 4713 weak rows. The sensor reports a distance even with no usable return; what produces it is not established.

tof_weak_distance_sd_mm.source: REC, REC2. Fitted by simulacrum/prox_fit.py to all 9929 state rows of the nine recordings that carry the sensor's distance and signal quality (one robot; what stood in front of it is not known). Spread of the weak rows' distance, from their quartiles (56 and 86 mm) as if normal. The real distribution has tails this leaves out: 6% of weak rows read 30 and 3% read 400.

tof_lift_quality.source: REC, REC2. Fitted by simulacrum/prox_fit.py to all 9929 state rows of the nine recordings that carry the sensor's distance and signal quality (one robot; what stood in front of it is not known). Median signal quality of the 111 rows with the lift in the beam that read the minimum distance.

motor_reference_voltage_v.source: REC: the battery read 4.10 V at the start and 3.96 V at the end, as the recording lane (a lane) reported them in commit 83326742b0; neither reading is in the recording files. The midpoint. The tread drive values (tread_noload_speed_mmps, wheel_stall_torque_mNm) were fitted to REC, so they hold at this voltage.
motor_reference_voltage_v.note: The drive is scaled by battery voltage over this (robot._drive_treads).

battery_rest_voltage_v.source: No source states the voltage of a given episode; the value equals motor_reference_voltage_v so the fitted drive is unchanged. The range is the SDK's: "fully-charged above 4.1 volts. At 3.6V, the robot is approaching low charge" (SDKPY, anki_vector/robot.py:765).
battery_rest_voltage_v.note: Drawn per episode in training. The tread drive's PWM duty is multiplied by this over motor_reference_voltage_v: lower voltage, lower stall torque and top speed; back-EMF damping unchanged.

battery_sag_v_per_power.source: No source. Drop of the battery's voltage per unit of summed tread duty (0..2). The SDK's get_battery_state cannot measure it: in REC2 run F it returned 4.0797 V unchanged 165 times over 2.5 min of full-power spins. A measurement needs the robot's own syscon reading at a higher rate, or a meter on the cell.

tread_heat_tau_s.source: REC2. Time constant of a tread motor's heat state. Fitted by simulacrum/motor_heat_fit.py to REC2 run F (unit 1, 29 full-power spins of 3 s at 300 mm/s commanded, 2 s rests, 150 s, ended by a cliff): per tread, the ceiling it reached after 1.5 s of each spin, against a first-order heat state that follows the duty. Fitted on cycles 0-9 (20 spins), held out cycles 10-14 (9 spins). Right tread: ceiling 251.0 forward and 244.2 back when cold, held-out error 1.9 mm/s against 8.5 for a constant ceiling. Left tread: held-out error 2.8 mm/s against 1.2 for a constant, so no heating is supported. The 150 s run does not pin the time constant: tau 40-600 s fit within 1.5x of the best error, trading against the loss; what it pins is the initial rate of loss. The SDK's battery reading did not move during the run, so voltage cannot be split out; the left tread holding its ceiling says the fall was in the right motor, not the battery. One unit, one run: 'multiple units' is not yet met. Best tau 85 s.

tread_heat_loss_rate_per_s.source: REC2. Left, right: the fraction of drive a cold tread loses per second at full duty; the loss at full heat is this times tread_heat_tau_s. Fitted by simulacrum/motor_heat_fit.py to REC2 run F (unit 1, 29 full-power spins of 3 s at 300 mm/s commanded, 2 s rests, 150 s, ended by a cliff): per tread, the ceiling it reached after 1.5 s of each spin, against a first-order heat state that follows the duty. Fitted on cycles 0-9 (20 spins), held out cycles 10-14 (9 spins). Right tread: ceiling 251.0 forward and 244.2 back when cold, held-out error 1.9 mm/s against 8.5 for a constant ceiling. Left tread: held-out error 2.8 mm/s against 1.2 for a constant, so no heating is supported. The 150 s run does not pin the time constant: tau 40-600 s fit within 1.5x of the best error, trading against the loss; what it pins is the initial rate of loss. The SDK's battery reading did not move during the run, so voltage cannot be split out; the left tread holding its ceiling says the fall was in the right motor, not the battery. One unit, one run: 'multiple units' is not yet met. Right 0.207 %/s at the best tau, 0.128-0.342 %/s across tau 40-600 s; left 0.062 %/s at the best tau but not supported by the held-out spins, so 0, with the fitted range above it.
tread_heat_loss_rate_per_s.note: Applied as a factor on the drive like the battery voltage (robot._drive_treads). Whether the model's ceiling falls by the same fraction as the drive is checked in tests (test_drive).

battery_voltage_v.note: The nominal figure; the model uses battery_rest_voltage_v.

servo_command_delay_ms.source: REC, REC2. Time from a head or lift command to the motor acting on it, return path included. Those commands are actions through the robot's engine, not direct motor commands. Fitted by fit_recording.py --servo-delay (2026-11-18, 19 replays, from 100 ms) to REC segments head_2, head_4 and lift_1 only, the head and lift ramped at head_accel_default_radps2 and lift_accel_default_radps2 with both caps at 10 rad/s: 105 ms, fit score 0.0327 (0.0327 at 100, 0.0329 at 95 and 110, 0.036 at 80, 0.034 at 125). Held out: REC head_3 and lift_2 score 0.0350, and all 15 head and lift moves of REC2 run A score 0.0317 (head 0.0308, lift 0.0328). With the constant-rate head and lift these replaced (no ramp, caps 1.75 and 2.8 rad/s, 225 ms) the same three scores are 0.0187, 0.0520 and 0.0598 (replay_recording.py, the ramp switched off with accelerations of 1e6; --servos-of for REC2). REC2 run A alone would choose 110-125 ms.

head_speed_max_radps.source: REC, REC2. A top rate on the head's ramp, below the max_speed the SDK asks for. With the ramp at head_accel_default_radps2 neither recording shows one: the longest move in REC2 run A (67 deg) peaks at about 3.4 rad/s on the ramp, and any cap above that gives the same replay, so the value is the SDK's requested 10 rad/s (SDKPY:684) and the low bound is the highest ramp peak seen. Fitting the cap together with the delay on REC alone gave 1.24 rad/s, which fitted REC's three fit segments better (0.026) and everything held out worse (REC 0.065, REC2 run A 0.081); it was not adopted. Fitted by fit_recording.py --servo-delay (2026-11-18, 19 replays, from 100 ms) to REC segments head_2, head_4 and lift_1 only, the head and lift ramped at head_accel_default_radps2 and lift_accel_default_radps2 with both caps at 10 rad/s: 105 ms, fit score 0.0327 (0.0327 at 100, 0.0329 at 95 and 110, 0.036 at 80, 0.034 at 125). Held out: REC head_3 and lift_2 score 0.0350, and all 15 head and lift moves of REC2 run A score 0.0317 (head 0.0308, lift 0.0328). With the constant-rate head and lift these replaced (no ramp, caps 1.75 and 2.8 rad/s, 225 ms) the same three scores are 0.0187, 0.0520 and 0.0598 (replay_recording.py, the ramp switched off with accelerations of 1e6; --servos-of for REC2). REC2 run A alone would choose 110-125 ms.

lift_speed_max_radps.source: REC, REC2. As head_speed_max_radps, for the lift arm's angle: no cap below the SDK's requested 10 rad/s (SDKPY:754) shows in either recording with the ramp in place; the low bound is the fastest arm rate seen between samples in REC (6.0 rad/s). Fitted by fit_recording.py --servo-delay (2026-11-18, 19 replays, from 100 ms) to REC segments head_2, head_4 and lift_1 only, the head and lift ramped at head_accel_default_radps2 and lift_accel_default_radps2 with both caps at 10 rad/s: 105 ms, fit score 0.0327 (0.0327 at 100, 0.0329 at 95 and 110, 0.036 at 80, 0.034 at 125). Held out: REC head_3 and lift_2 score 0.0350, and all 15 head and lift moves of REC2 run A score 0.0317 (head 0.0308, lift 0.0328). With the constant-rate head and lift these replaced (no ramp, caps 1.75 and 2.8 rad/s, 225 ms) the same three scores are 0.0187, 0.0520 and 0.0598 (replay_recording.py, the ramp switched off with accelerations of 1e6; --servos-of for REC2). REC2 run A alone would choose 110-125 ms.

cliff_reaction_pause_ms.source: REC, one event: the cliff bit first shows at t = 159.734 s and the treads move again between 160.928 and 160.983 s, so 1.19 to 1.25 s after it. The firmware's 500 ms cliff event delay (FW:331) is not this pause.

lift_arm_mass_fraction.source: No source. Share of the lift mass in the arms; the rest is the fork.

head_angle_tol_deg.source: FW:32 HEAD_ANGLE_TOL = 2 degrees ("within this tolerance of the target angle, it is done moving")

heading_hold_gain_mmps_per_rad.source: No source. Wheel speed difference per radian of heading error in a straight drive; stands in for the firmware path follower.

drive_done_mm.source: No source. Remaining distance at which a straight drive ends.

contact_time_constant_ms.source: Solver setting. Stiffness of the contact model; at least two timesteps. A convergence check, not an unknown about the robot: rank_assumed.py reports what moving it does.

tip_support_clearance_mm.source: Modelling setting. How far the body-fixed tip supports round the real axles sit above the table at rest (simulacrum/mjcf.py, _tip_supports_xml): enough that they carry nothing on a flat table, small enough that they take over as soon as the body tilts a few degrees. They exist only when tread_contact_inset_mm is above 0.

tip_supports_driven.source: Modelling setting. 1 puts each tip support (tip_support_clearance_mm) on its own hinge geared to its tread, so its surface moves at tread speed, as the real tread does where it wraps the axle; 0 keeps them fixed to the body. Unit 3 wheelstands W4 and W8 (evidence/unit3-wheelstand/reproduction): with 0, peak pitch stays at or below 47 degrees at every lift torque cap tried from 30 to 250 mN m, against 72.3 and 72.5 degrees measured; with 1 it passes 72 degrees from 100 mN m. Off by default: on the flat the supports do not touch, but the added joints change the solver's numbers, and the fitted tread values were fitted with 0.

settle_time_ms.source: Solver setting. Time the model is stepped at rest before the clock starts.

table_length_mm.source: Scenario setting, not a property of the robot. Measure the real table to train for one table; the range trains for many.

sim_timestep_ms.source: Solver setting. A convergence check: rank_assumed.py reports what halving it does.

missing.name: overall_envelope_mm
missing.what: Length, width and height of the whole robot, lift down and head level.
missing.measure: Ruler or calipers on the robot standing on a flat surface.

missing.name: total_mass_g
missing.what: Mass of the robot. The table carries an assumed 170 g.

missing.name: centre_of_mass
missing.what: Fore-aft and vertical position of the centre of mass. Assumed.
missing.measure: Balance the robot on a straight edge laid across the treads and mark the balance line; repeat on its side.

missing.name: part_masses_and_inertia
missing.what: Mass of head, lift, wheels and their inertia. Assumed.
missing.measure: Not measurable without taking the robot apart. To be fitted from recorded motion.

missing.name: gear_ratio_and_encoder_slots
missing.what: Gear ratios and encoder counts per motor turn. The firmware gives tread travel per count (0.1269 mm) but not what its divisors 172.3, 149.7 and 366.211 are.
missing.measure: Check the odometry scale instead: a timed, taped drive of a known distance.
missing.needs: timed drive on a barriered surface

missing.name: motor_torque_curve
missing.what: Stall force of the tread motors. The recording fixes the motor's strength relative to the load (stall torque against rotor inertia, mass and friction), not the torque itself; the table's 100 mN*m is a fit with the assumed mass in place.
missing.measure: Push against a force gauge at a low commanded speed; time drives at several speeds.
missing.needs: force gauge, timed drive on a barriered surface

missing.name: wheel_speed_response
missing.what: The true top speed and the response above 100 mm/s. The recording covers spins at 30, 60 and 100 mm/s and straight steps of 0.4 and 0.7 s at 40 and 80 mm/s, too short to reach a steady speed. The no-load speed in the table is a fit to those and is an extrapolation above 100 mm/s.
missing.measure: Step the wheel speed and log the reported wheel speeds at the state rate.
missing.needs: timed drive on a barriered surface

missing.name: tread_friction
missing.what: Friction of the treads on the surface in use. Assumed 0.9.
missing.measure: Tilt the surface with the robot on it, treads held, until it slides; the coefficient is the tangent of the angle.
missing.needs: a board and a protractor or phone inclinometer

missing.name: turn_slip
missing.what: Why the robot turns at about half the no-slip rate, and what it does above 100 mm/s. In the recording the six spins at 30, 60 and 100 mm/s turn at 0.44 to 0.53 of the no-slip rate (mean 0.50, from gyro x and z together; the head-mounted gyro's z axis alone reads 0.41 to 0.50 because the head was 22 deg up). The model gives 0.44 to 0.46: it turns about 8 percent slower than the robot did. In the model the figure follows mostly from the assumed centre of mass, which is not measured; it is not fitted to this one number, because several unknowns move it. Not recorded: a held spin above 100 mm/s, a turn count against a mark on the surface, a spin with the head level. The robot's own turn after its cliff reaction touched 210 to 235 mm/s for three samples (0.12 s) at 276 to 301 deg/s, 0.49 to 0.56 of no-slip; the firmware's 360 deg/s figure would need 0.66.
missing.measure: Measure the centre of mass first (see centre_of_mass). Then command equal and opposite wheel speeds for a fixed time with the head level, in both directions, and count turns against a mark; an overhead video gives the turn centre as well.
missing.needs: timed turns on a barriered surface, a mark, and a phone camera overhead

missing.name: cliff_sensor_height_and_range
missing.what: Height of the cliff sensors and the drop at which the cliff bit sets. Assumed.
missing.measure: Raise the robot on shims of known thickness until the cliff bit sets; measure the sensor windows with a ruler.

missing.name: cliff_reaction
missing.what: The robot's own reaction at more than one speed. One event is recorded (54 mm/s, during the robot's own drive back to the charger): pause 1.19 to 1.25 s, 29 mm away at about 205 mm/s by the robot's odometry. Not recorded: where the front axle stops relative to the edge, and any speed above 54 mm/s.
missing.measure: At the default control level, drive at a low step edge at several speeds and tape the stop point and the back-up.
missing.needs: timed drive at a low step on a barriered surface

missing.name: command_delay
missing.what: Delay from an SDK command to motion, apart from the delay of the state message coming back. The recording has host times only, so the table's 60 ms is the two together, and 60 and 80 ms fit equally well at a 60 ms state period.
missing.measure: Log the robot's own timestamp for each state message beside the host's receive time, if the SDK exposes one; or film the treads with the host clock in frame.
missing.needs: timed drive on a barriered surface

missing.name: tof_noise_and_bias
missing.what: Bias of the forward range reading, and its noise at more than one distance. Measured at one distance only (237 mm, standard deviation 5.2 mm, robot asleep on the charger).
missing.measure: Read the range at taped distances from a flat target.

missing.name: imu_orientation_noise_bias
missing.what: Noise of the IMU while awake and moving, the roll of its frame, and its scale. Now in the table from the recording: its axes turn with the head, its frame is pitched about -0.7 deg, the accelerometer's steady offsets (fitted), and the gyro's residual offset while still (measured). Still missing: noise is measured asleep on the charger only; a roll of the frame cannot be told from the y offset; scale errors cannot be told from offsets with gravity as the only reference.
missing.measure: Log the IMU at rest with the robot on each of its sides and on its back, on a surface checked with a level; log it while driving on the surface in use.
missing.needs: a level surface and a spirit level

missing.name: cube_mass_g
missing.what: Mass of the light cube with its cell. Assumed 50 g.

missing.name: cube_chip_place
missing.what: Where the cube's accelerometer sits in the cube and which way its x axis points. Assumed at the centre, axes unknown.
missing.measure: Spin tests with the cube in the lift, recorded by hardware/cube_accel.py (README).

missing.name: cube_accel_offset_and_scale
missing.what: The cube accelerometer's zero-g offset and scale per axis. Assumed nominal.
missing.measure: Record the cube still on each of its six faces on a level surface.
missing.needs: a powered cube and a level surface

missing.name: cube_tick_period
missing.what: The cube app's true tick period: 10 ms plus the tick's own run time.
missing.measure: Any recording by hardware/cube_accel.py: one message per three ticks.
